minor.issue: Brute-force lockout uses request.client.host which behind k8s ingress resolves to per-pod internal IPs (e.g. 10.227.4.133 and 10.227.51.104). Each attacker request is round-robin'd across backend pods, so lockout key becomes ip:email per-pod. Real external attacker from a single client IP gets 5 attempts × N pods before lockout (observed ~10 attempts with 2 pods). Fix: honor X-Forwarded-For (or ingress client IP header) as the identifier instead of request.client.host.

action_items: Change brute-force lockout identifier in /app/backend/auth.py from request.client.host to X-Forwarded-For (first hop) so limits are per real client IP instead of per internal pod IP. Currently the lockout is effectively 5*N (N = replicas) attempts per email per attacker IP.
critical_code_review_comments: auth.py _check_lockout/_record_failed_login: identifier `request.client.host:email` under ingress/LB is the internal pod IP. This causes per-pod partitioning of lockout state and multiplies allowed attempts by replica count. Use `request.headers.get('x-forwarded-for','').split(',')[0].strip() or request.client.host` as identifier prefix.

rca of the issue: Brute-force lockout ineffective under k8s multi-pod: request.client.host in FastAPI returns the direct connection peer, which behind an ingress/LB is a per-pod internal IP (10.227.4.133, 10.227.51.104 observed). Since the lockout key is `client.host:email`, each replica pod keeps its own counter and an attacker's requests are load-balanced across pods, so they get MAX_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS × pod_count attempts before the first pod that reaches 5 will 429 — and even then, the next request may hit an unlocked pod. Mitigation: derive client IP from X-Forwarded-For (or a trusted proxy header) and use that as the lockout key, so all replicas share the same identifier for a given attacker.
